Navigating Dining Out from the Dietary Guidance & Support pillar: how the program teaches it, one practical idea, no rules or numbers.

Going out to eat doesn't have to feel stressful or lead to a spiral. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, Navigating Dining Out is part of our Dietary Guidance & Support pillar. Our registered dietitians work with clients to build skills that make restaurants feel enjoyable again, not triggering or forbidden. One simple approach: before you go, decide what kind of experience you want. Not what you'll order, but how you want to feel when you leave. Satisfied? Comfortable? Connected to the people you're with? That intention becomes your guide, not a set of food rules. We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes and movement education in one program. San Antonio and virtual across Texas. Link in the first comment.

Coordination with the referring provider and the discharge summary of behavioral progress (assessment scores: nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, depression). LinkedIn document post, Todd's sentences verbatim.

When you refer a patient to the Bariatric Counseling Center, you receive consistent coordination throughout their care and a detailed discharge summary at program completion.

Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics.

The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four.

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. We accept most health insurances.

San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

Stress eating as a pattern, not a character flaw; coping skills the program teaches. Mention the day once.

A long day doesn't make stress eating inevitable. When evening becomes the only quiet moment, reaching for food makes sense, but there are other ways to find that same comfort.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we teach coping skills that work when the day has worn you down. Our clients learn to recognize patterns, not judge them. They build a toolkit of responses that don't involve the kitchen or the drive-through.

Behavioral therapy. Dietary guidance. Culinary classes. Mindful movement. One program, not four.

Serving clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas.
